items.title: Google fined $463 million over E.U. location data violations
items.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission found Google mishandled location data across three features from 2018 to 2020

items.title: Google & Apple hunt for crypto talent
items.summary: Google and Apple are both hiring for digital-asset roles, from tokenizing real-world assets in Asia to Apple Pay strategy, a sign that stablecoins and tokenization are becoming core expertise inside Big Tech. CoinDesk's Uyen Truong hosts "CoinDesk Daily."

items.title: Takeaways for banks from Walmart's about-face on Apple and Google wallets
items.summary: Payment experts say that in the wake of Walmart supporting more digital wallets, many banks are missing the boat with mobile wallets by not aiming to stay top-of-wallet and by ignoring operational issues.

items.title: Target Uses AI Personalization to Deepen Digital Guest Engagement
items.summary: Target banks on AI personalization, wish lists and external platform partnerships to boost digital discovery, engagement and conversion.

items.title: Apple and Google Go Hunting for Crypto Talent, Hint at Stablecoin Push
items.summary: The senior roles cover Apple’s consumer payment products and Google Cloud’s institutional blockchain business in Asia.

items.title: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Surges As Alphabet, Nvidia Pop; Bessent Touts This China AI Maneuver (Live Coverage)
items.summary: The Dow Jones index rallies on the stock market today after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent touts China talks. Nvidia stock climbs.

items.title: Is It Too Late To Buy Microsoft Stock After Its Summer Run?
items.summary: Microsoft (MSFT) stock is up about 30% in three months, including a 19% jump in the two trading days after its July report. That makes buying now feel late. Yet the stock is slightly lower than a year ago, while the S&P 500 (SPY) gained about 17%. With the stock trading near $500 a share, Wall Street consensus is already banking on Microsoft beating its own forecast again.

items.title: AMD Stock’s Relentless Rally Pushes It Into The Trillion-Dollar Club, Albeit Briefly – Chip Stocks Light Up Wall Street
items.summary: The semiconductor rally came alongside a roughly 3% decline in U.S. crude prices and lower Treasury yields, helping lift broader U.S. equity indexes.
